record.interface_detail: wrangler deploy plus a 12 MB Go bridge
record.tooling: Go bridge plus pnpm and wrangler; a CA certificate must be installed on each device
record.chaining: composes with a Cloudflare account and a paid Workers plan, and with cloudflare-tunnel only if the Worker is fronted by one.

limits.value: no figure stated; the Workers paid plan is billed per request and duration beyond the included allowance

record.binding_note: the Worker sits in the data path and every datagram becomes Worker work, so the plan's request and duration billing is what fails first at sustained volume; the README states no figure for it

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account on the Workers paid plan at $5/mo, which needs a payment method

record.reliability_note: the Worker terminates and re-originates TLS, so every upstream connection is intercepted by design; single maintainer, no releases
record.confidence_note: Workers-based proxy architecture and WebSocket encapsulation are documented in project source code.

evidence.proved: "Cloudflare account (Workers paid plan, $5/mo)" in the prerequisites
the architecture line: stock WireGuard client, Go bridge over a single WebSocket, Durable Object, TLS MITM, then fetch() upstream
2 stars, no releases, last push 2026-04-06; the description calls it "Very rough"

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 5 per month, Workers paid plan
record.notes: Experimental proxy design routing WireGuard connections through Cloudflare Workers. Requires paid Cloudflare Workers subscriptions for WebSocket and network routing.

extras.wg_detail: device runs a stock WireGuard client against localhost:51820, a Go bridge (wireguard-go plus gvisor netstack) forwards over one WebSocket to a Cloudflare Durable Object
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the Worker plan is priced per month, not per byte, and the README states no transfer figure
extras.transit_note: through a Cloudflare Durable Object, which sees the plaintext of every intercepted connection
extras.hosting_requirement: no locally owned host, but a Cloudflare Workers paid plan at $5/mo, and a device able to run the Go bridge
